page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-176 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor. It features 176 vCPUs mapped to 88 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1408.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 146,417.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 104,670.37. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 11,970.86 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 446.56 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The architecture supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, which drive top-tier results in specialized workloads like ray tracing and image processing. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,723.0 and moderate single-threaded compression speeds.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highmem-176 offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with a high vCPU count on a single dedicated hypervisor node. This configuration minimizes inter-node latency for large-scale applications, though the lack of bundled local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which may introduce I/O latency tradeoffs.

This server is highly suited for memory-intensive and compute-heavy enterprise workloads. Appropriate applications include large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, which achieved 164.09 million operations per second in testing, high-throughput static web serving, complex database operations, software compilation, and data-dense parallel processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-176 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C x86_64 processor, it delivers 176 vCPUs across 88 physical cores with a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, paired with 1408.0 GB of RAM. While it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, the instance excels in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth, achieving top-tier benchmark results in stress-ng multi-core tests and uncached memory reads. It features Intel AVX-512 and AMX extensions, enhancing performance for vector and matrix operations. Qualitatively, the server provides high resource density for massive datasets, though workloads requiring high-speed local I/O must account for the lack of local SSDs. It is highly suited for in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, and parallel data processing.
